data.title: OpenAI-Compatible API
data.tagline: A third-party model endpoint conforming to OpenAI request and response formats, allowing compatible clients to switch providers seamlessly.
data.learningOutcome: You can separate protocol compatibility from model capability and test the features your tool actually needs.
data.description: For example, a tool that only sends OpenAI-shaped requests may connect to another model service after changing the Base URL, API key, and model name. The service may implement that shape directly or through a translation layer. Compatibility usually covers only some endpoints and fields, so tool calls, images, streaming, and other capabilities still need separate checks.

learning.assumes: You know that APIs agree on a shape for requests and responses.
learning.outcome: You can separate protocol compatibility from model capability and test the features your tool actually needs.

distinctions.label: Base URL
distinctions.explanation: A Base URL is the network root prefix of a server; an OpenAI-Compatible API specifies the protocol schema and message format used over that connection.

explanation.title: The tool sends a familiar request
explanation.text: The tool sends a request with familiar paths and fields, so connecting to different model services looks similar.

explanation.title: The model service generates the result
explanation.text: The model service receives the request, processes it, and generates the answer. Different services may use different models and processing rules.

explanation.title: Check each capability separately
explanation.text: For example, a text-only model may accept an image field without being able to understand the image. Tool calls and streaming also need separate tests.

data.boundary: An OpenAI-compatible API is a communication convention, not an OpenAI GPT model. It standardizes communication format; it does not mean the underlying model has OpenAI model capabilities such as tool calling, multimodal input, or streaming.

lessonPractice.title: The endpoint is compatible, but the model says it does not support tool calls. Which judgment is correct?

options.label: Protocol compatibility does not mean the underlying model supports tool calls
options.feedback: Correct. A compatible API standardizes request packaging; tool calls still depend on the model.

options.label: A compatible endpoint must provide every capability of a GPT model
options.feedback: Protocol and model capability are different layers; compatibility does not guarantee identical tool, multimodal, or streaming behavior.

options.label: A configuration flag can add tool-calling capability that the model does not have
options.feedback: A setting can request a capability, but it cannot give the model the ability to understand tools and emit structured arguments.

data.agentPrompt: Check which OpenAI-compatible endpoints the tool and model service both support, then use non-sensitive requests to test ordinary chat and tool calling separately. Record the actual URL, status code, and missing capabilities without printing the real key.
